<SUMMARY>The period of February 27 - March 6, 2026, was dominated by escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia, particularly the ongoing conflict involving Iran, Israel, and the United States. This conflict resulted in significant market volatility, driving up oil and gas prices and disrupting supply chains globally, including a declaration of force majeure on gasoline exports by India and warnings from South Korea regarding chipmaking material disruptions. Concurrently, major developments in AI chip technology and data center infrastructure were observed, with Broadcom projecting substantial growth and Intel's Foundry division nearing a significant advanced packaging deal. Critical mineral security remained a high priority, evidenced by US efforts in Venezuela and Japan's initiatives in Africa. State actions included new trade deals for India and Canada, and China's continued focus on technological self-reliance.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>South Korea warned of potential disruption to the supply of key chipmaking materials. The ongoing conflict in West Asia presents significant risks to global energy security, manifested in severely reduced movement through the Strait of Hormuz due to war cover cancellations by insurers, soaring European gas benchmarks, and tanker rate increases. Pakistan's conflict with Afghanistan's Taliban leadership has halted critical Central Asian trade routes, posing further regional instability. The substantial energy and water demands of AI data centers represent a growing challenge.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
China set its lowest growth target in decades, aiming for 4.5% to 5%. Broadcom reported its AI chip revenue more than doubled in the latest quarter and projects sales to exceed $100 billion by 2027 due to robust custom chip demand. Intel's Foundry division is near a deal for its advanced packaging technology, expected to contribute billions of dollars annually. CDT presented a summary of content blocked or deleted from Chinese platforms in January 2026. South Korea stocks crashed 18% in two days. AZ officials inked an agreement with Japan to foster semiconductor and trade collaboration. Nvidia suspended H200 AI chip production for the China market. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) shares decreased by 1.1%.

**Africa:**
Taara, a Google X spinoff, debuted a new product at Mobile World Congress in Barcelona, aiming to bring fiber-optic speeds to open-air laser links in sub-Saharan Africa. The Federal Government of Nigeria intensified efforts to reposition the country as a continental industrial hub, with the Minister of Steel Development, Shuaibu Audu, declaring Nigeria is ready to move beyond raw material exports and is seeking credit and long-term German investment for its $10 billion steel industry.

**Europe:**
Finland's economy emerged from recession in the final quarter of 2025 and shifted to a modest growth path, with Danske Bank forecasting a further pickup in coming years. Biomemory acquired Catalog Technologies, gaining key patents and infrastructure for DNA data storage development. European shares rallied after two days of heavy losses.

**Americas:**
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated he couldn’t rule out his country’s military participation in the escalating war in West Asia. Executives from Google LLC, Microsoft Corp., Amazon.com Inc., Meta, Oracle, OpenAI, and xAI met with President Donald Trump at the White House and signed a "rate payer protection pledge" to bear the cost of new electricity generation for their data centers. Hundreds of employees at Google and OpenAI signed a public letter urging their companies to set firm boundaries on how AI can be used by the military. A class action lawsuit was filed against CoreWeave, Inc., with a lead plaintiff deadline of March 13, 2026.
</EXEC>
<LITHO></LITHO>
<REE>
**Asia:**
China's top chip bosses urged supportive policies to create a domestic "ASML," and China seeks to enhance its rare earth advantages, implementing "extraordinary measures" to achieve semiconductor breakthroughs, as indicated in a new five-year plan focused on technological self-reliance.

**Africa:**
The Federal Government of Nigeria is seeking long-term German investment to develop its $10 billion steel industry. Japan aims to develop rare earth mines in Africa to reduce its reliance on China.

**Europe:**
Rare Earths Norway reported that the estimate of Europe's biggest deposit increased by 81%.

**Americas:**
US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum visited Caracas, pushing for greater access to critical minerals, with US mining companies lining up to invest in Venezuela. USA Rare Earth announced its acquisition of Texas Mineral Resources Corp. for $73 million, consolidating control of the Round Top project.

**Oceania:**
A report highlighted the unlikelihood of the US curtailing China's dominance over critical minerals, noting China's control of over 80% of global battery production. Australia is strengthening transparency and security for its rare earth supply chains to the United States. Australia and Vietnam are working towards building a strong rare earth partnership.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
China's state media reported a 4.5% to 5% growth target for the economy, a downgrade from the "around 5%" set in the past three years. The "404 Deleted Content Archive" for January 2026 provided a summary of censored content from Chinese platforms like WeChat and Weibo. South Korea warned of potential disruption to key chipmaking materials.

**Americas:**
US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum visited Caracas, pushing for greater access to Venezuelan critical minerals, with US mining companies preparing for investments. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada cannot rule out military participation in the conflict in West Asia.

**Oceania:**
La Trobe University appointed Macquarie University's AI chief as a pro vice-chancellor focused solely on AI. Intel Chairman Frank Yeary retired, with Craig Barrat set to become the new chairman of the Board of Directors.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Americas:**
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated his country might participate militarily in the escalating conflict in West Asia. Nvidia is hiring an "Orbital Datacenter System Architect" to define and build products for AI in orbit, suggesting the company is exploring space-based data centers.

**Europe:**
B-2 stealth bombers are scheduled to land at UK bases, specifically RAF Fairford and Diego Garcia, in days, signaling an escalation in US-Israel operations.

**Asia:**
The Pakistan-Afghanistan conflict, largely overlooked due to the burgeoning conflict in West Asia, has erupted along their southern rim, representing a major setback for Central Asia’s global trade agenda.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>The global geopolitical landscape remains highly volatile, driven primarily by the escalating conflict in West Asia and its widespread economic ramifications, including disruptions to energy markets and supply chains. Simultaneously, the accelerating development and adoption of AI technologies are reshaping industrial strategies and infrastructure demands across all regions, prompting both significant investment and ethical considerations regarding military applications. Strategic competition for critical minerals underscores ongoing efforts by various nations to secure vital resources and reduce reliance on single dominant suppliers.</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Hanmi Semiconductor strengthened ties with India amid the launch of a Micron facility, with the South Korean company developing a dual-function BOC COB Bonder capable of both Board-on-Chip (BOC) and Chip-on-Board (COB) processes. India is actively seeking semiconductor investments from Dutch firms, offering substantial subsidies to attract chip manufacturing, anticipating a strategic partnership. Canada and India signed a landmark uranium deal worth $2.6 billion, as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney encouraged trade with nations other than the United States. India is aiming to become a global hub for artificial intelligence and cloud computing infrastructure, actively wooing global tech companies, but faces challenges from the enormous energy and water demands of AI data centers. Indian state-run refiner Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) declared force majeure on all planned gasoline export cargoes for March and April due to the Middle East conflict halting crude supply out of the Gulf. China and Russia are observing the "next level nature" of US and Israel tech-enhanced intelligence and drones integrated into combined operations.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
Iran launched a massive retaliatory campaign, deploying over 500 ballistic missiles and 2,000 drones across targets in Israel and several Gulf states, following joint U.S. and Israeli airstrikes. A drone strike on a command center in Iran was reported. The conflict significantly reduced movement through the Strait of Hormuz due to war cover cancellations by insurers, causing tanker rates to surge and oil prices to fly. The Iran conflict upended the LNG market, jolting gas prices, and sent the European Title Transfer Facility (TTF) benchmark soaring. Panic selling was observed in Asian markets. AWS data centers in the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain were damaged or directly hit by drones, with Amazon stating the Bahrain facility was impacted by a nearby drone strike. Pentagon's Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the United States military killed an Iranian official linked to a plot against President Donald Trump, with US strikes expanding further into Iran. Israel launched fresh Iran strikes, leading to a surge in evacuation flights from the region. NATO intercepted a missile over northeastern Syria that was heading for Turkey. China expressed anger over US-Israel strikes on Iran but indicated it would not risk its interests by confronting Washington. The Senate rejected a Democratic-led Iran war powers resolution that called for congressional approval for military action against Iran. The Pakistan-Afghanistan conflict erupted along its southern rim, halting critical Central Asian trade routes. South Korea warned that the Iran crisis could disrupt the supply of key chipmaking materials. Rare Earth Stocks, including REalloys, saw increased demand as the conflict escalated.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The ongoing kinetic conflict in West Asia will continue to be a primary driver of global instability, impacting energy markets, supply chains, and international trade dynamics. The intensified focus on AI and advanced semiconductor technologies, coupled with the critical minerals race, will likely accelerate strategic alliances and investments while simultaneously presenting vulnerabilities to disruptions. Nations will increasingly prioritize supply chain resilience and diversification, particularly in high-tech and resource sectors, against a backdrop of evolving geopolitical alignments and domestic economic priorities.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
